discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 160943
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
543 AM EDT Fri Oct 16 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Turning much cooler and windy for today with lake effect rain
  showers expected. The strongest wind gusts are expected 
  downwind of Lake Michigan across Berrien and La Porte Counties
  where gusts to 45 mph are likely Friday afternoon and 
  evening. A wind advisory has been hoisted as a result.

- Chances for frost are best on Saturday night, however some 
  frost cannot be ruled out tonight.

- After below normal temperatures this weekend, temperatures
  will warm back above normal early next week. Additionally, dry
  weather looks to persist through much of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 257 AM EDT Fri Oct 16 2026

As a mid level trough digs across the Central US, an upper low gets 
shoved northeastward pushing a surface low into southeast 
Canada/Northeast US. At the same time, a 1040 mb surface high slides 
southeastward into the Central CONUS. The presence of this strong 
surface high often indicates the arrival of a cooler airmass and 
that is the case this time. Given our departure of above normal 
temperatures and the arrival of this cool airmass, we'll have some 
hazards to contend with today and this weekend. First, yesterday's 
cold front shifts eastward and the vigorous vort max associated with 
the mid level trough dives through Lk MI late this afternoon into 
this evening. Given the warm lake and the 850 mb temps dipping to 
around or below 0C, lake enhancement is expected to cause rain.
A surface trough is expected to swing through the southeast 
area of Lk MI around 18z with ample low level moisture, low 
level wind convergence, and building lake enhanced instability. 
Given the movement of this trough and swiveling trajectories 
from northwest to north, the area with the best chance to see 
"higher" QPF is southern Berrien into LaPorte where 0.25 to 0.5"
is forecast, tapering off the farther away from the lake you 
are. The heaviest of the rain appears to get into Berrien county
midday (15 or 16z) and continues swiveling southward through 
the afternoon and into the evening. The other hazard is wind 
gusts, which look to get underway along lk MI- adjacent 
locations around 19 or 20z before pulling away around 3z. Given 
the surface trough, there could be some isentropic downglide 
enough to work an isolated 45 kt gust down to the surface. 
Otherwise, it appears that frequent gusts between 30 and 40 mph 
will be possible during that time as low level lapse rates 
become conducive. The strongest of the gusts are adjacent to the
lake, tapering off the farther away you get. This is why the 
wind advisory was hoisted for Lk MI- adjacent locales. 

The mention of the cold air also brings to mind the chance for 
frost. Especially with overnight lows dropping into the 30s from 
from tonight/Sat AM to Sunday night/Mon AM and potentially 
again Tue AM. The main issue with Friday night/Sat AM is the 
gradient which could keep winds strong enough to eliminate 
formation of frost. A lesser possibility is lake clouds hang on,
but would probably lean towards subsidence on the eastern side 
of the lake clouds removing them. Clouds appear to already be 
dissipating on the NAM by around 6 to 9z for maybe all of our 
counties (lowest confidence on LaPorte to White county line).
This would give areas along or about IN-15 north of US-24 on 
into MI the best chance to see frost tonight. Surface high 
pressure continues to poke into the area Saturday morning with 
the stronger gradient lurking to our north. So, cloud cover 
appears less of factor. It's often that as return flow begins to
occur that we get our best frost chances as winds slacken, but 
the boundary layer is able to get back to what it was the 
previous night or potentially colder. So, Saturday night has the
best chance for frost. There is also the possibility of a 
freeze primarily along and south of US-24 Sun AM with a couple 
hours of temps right around there then.

Surface high pressure then becomes stagnant across the eastern CONUS 
as blocking builds across the Atlantic. The NAO/AO both drop 
negative during this time. The upper jet also retreats back up into 
Canada. A slow moving trough moves into the western CONUS, but takes 
its time arriving into the area potentially continuing to provide 
dry weather into next weekend. Temperatures trend warmer with highs 
returning to the 70s during the next work week and lows warming 
slowly through the 40s.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 543 AM EDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Post-frontal cold advection will keep mainly MVFR cigs and gusty 
west-northwest winds going today. A digging upper level trough and 
associated secondary low level trough sink south through the area 
this afternoon bringing increasing chances for showers and vis 
restrictions, particularly at KSBN where there will be lake 
enhancement. This transitions to pure lake effect this evening at 
KSBN with additional shower chances and high MVFR cigs. Winds remain 
gusty and veer more northerly otherwise later this afternoon and 
evening.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Wind Advisory from 1 PM this afternoon to 10 PM CDT this 
     evening for INZ103-203.
OH...None.
MI...Wind Advisory from 2 PM this afternoon to 11 PM EDT this 
     evening for MIZ177-277.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 11 AM EDT this morning for LMZ043-
     046.
     Gale Warning from 11 AM this morning to 2 AM EDT Saturday for 
     LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.summary: Thunderstorms with wind-damage and localized brief-tornado potential are expected across parts of the Mid-Atlantic into southern New England, mainly this afternoon and early evening.
spc.text:
SPC AC 160556

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1256 AM CDT Fri Oct 16 2026

   Valid 161200Z - 171200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF THE
   MID-ATLANTIC INTO SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with wind-damage and localized brief-tornado potential
   are expected across parts of the Mid-Atlantic into southern New
   England, mainly this afternoon and early evening.

   ...Mid-Atlantic into southern New England...
   A deep, positive-tilt mid/upper-level trough is forecast to further
   amplify as it spreads over the eastern CONUS today. A surface low
   initially near the lower Great Lakes will move quickly eastward
   toward northern New England by evening. A trailing cold front will
   sweep through the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast from this afternoon
   into tonight. 

   In the wake of early-day clouds and precipitation, seasonably rich
   low-level moisture and modest diurnal heating will result in
   sufficient destabilization for storm development along the front.
   Very weak lapse rates above 500 mb will constrain MLCAPE magnitudes
   to the 500-1000 J/kg range, and result in rather low-topped
   convection. However, in areas where temperatures can rise to
   near/above 70 F, relatively robust buoyancy near/below 500 mb
   (characterized by lifted indices in the -4 to -6 C range) will
   develop prior to the frontal passage. This buoyancy will be
   sufficient for development of occasionally organized storm
   structures, in the presence of strengthening deep-layer flow/shear.
   35-45 kt of flow in the 1-2 km AGL layer will support potential for
   strong/damaging gusts with any sufficiently robust convection.  

   Generally front-parallel flow may result in a primarily linear mode
   as convective coverage increases, though 40+ kt of effective shear
   will support potential for embedded low-topped supercells. A
   localized wind-damage threat may develop early this afternoon from
   WV/western PA into southern NY, with initial frontal development.
   The wind-damage threat is expected to increase through the afternoon
   as storms spread eastward into a somewhat warmer and more unstable
   environment across eastern PA, NJ, and vicinity. Rather strong
   low-level shear will also support some brief-tornado potential with
   QLCS circulations and/or embedded supercell structures. 

   Some wind-damage potential could spread into southern New England by
   this evening, though marine-influenced low-level stability should
   eventually constrain the eastward extent of the threat.

   ..Dean/Chalmers.. 10/16/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 160524

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1224 AM CDT Fri Oct 16 2026

   Valid 171200Z - 181200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe weather is expected tomorrow (Saturday).

   ...Synopsis...
   Upper ridging and a surface anticyclone will overspread most of the
   CONUS as an upper trough ejects into the Atlantic tomorrow
   (Saturday). A relatively cool, stable airmass accompanying the
   surface anticyclone will suppress thunderstorm development over most
   locales. A surface cold front associated with the exiting upper
   trough will sweep across the FL Peninsula during the day, providing
   enough lift of a preceding moist airmass to support a couple of
   thunderstorms. Scant buoyancy, driven by cooler mid-level
   temperatures, will accompany a mid-level impulse over the Lower
   Colorado River Basin, where enough lift may be present to support a
   few lightning flashes.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/16/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 160649

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0149 AM CDT Fri Oct 16 2026

   Valid 181200Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected anywhere across the Contiguous
   United States on Sunday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Upper ridging will prevail across the central CONUS as a weak 500 mb
   cutoff low meanders off of the East Coast and broad, low-amplitude
   upper troughing dominates the Interior West on Sunday. A surface
   anticyclone will overspread the CONUS east of the MS River while
   surface troughing occurs across the Great Plains. Despite this
   surface troughing, medium-range guidance shows moist trajectories
   across the Gulf oriented away from the U.S. shoreline, suggesting
   that a stable airmass will remain over the CONUS. Therefore,
   thunderstorm potential should be hindered over most locales. The one
   exception may be southern FL into the Keys, where lingering
   low-level moisture in a post-cold-frontal airmass may support
   isolated thunderstorm development during the afternoon.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/16/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
